title: Royal Caribbean Internship 2027–2028: Programs, Deadlines & How to Apply
summary: Everything you need to land a Royal Caribbean internship in 2027–2028, programs, eligibility, deadlines, the interview process, and tips from past interns.
body_text: Royal Caribbean Internship 2027–2028: Programs, Deadlines & How to Apply Last updated: July 2026 Royal Caribbean Group runs one of the most competitive internship programs in the travel industry, with fewer than 5% of corporate applicants landing one of roughly 80–100 summer seats across a fleet that spans 69 ships, 1,000+ destinations, and all 7 continents. And the reviews back it up: Vault ranked the program #1 Best Travel & Transportation Internship for 2026 , while the company made Fortune's World's Most Admired Companies list for the first time . For the summer 2027 cycle, postings are expected to start going live in August–September 2026, with rolling review that closes positions when filled. Miss the first few weeks and you may miss the year. Quick Facts Fact Detail Where to apply careers.royalcaribbeangroup.com intern program . Filter for "Students & Recent Grads" on the job board Application window (2027) Expected August–November 2026 (first wave) and January–April 2027 (second wave) for summer 2027 (documented pattern; not yet posted) Rolling? Yes. Applications are "reviewed on a rolling basis" and positions "may close before the stated closing date" Eligibility Enrolled in a 4-year Bachelor's or Graduate program; expected graduation Dec 2027 or May 2028; US work authorization required (no H-1B sponsorship; CPT/OPT accepted) Duration 10 weeks (early June to early August); hybrid format, in-person Mon–Thu, remote Fridays Compensation $21–$24/hr official (undergraduate); Glassdoor averages ~$33/hr for technical roles; $1,000–$2,000 relocation stipend for non-local interns Return offers ~60–70% of strong performers receive full-time Analyst or Associate offers (community-reported, not official) Locations Miami, FL (PortMiami campus HQ) and Miramar, FL (Tech Hub) # Programs 10+ departments: Technology, Finance, Data Analytics & AI, Supply Chain, Marketing, Hospitality, and more The two numbers that matter: a rolling window expected to open August–September 2026 for summer 2027, and fewer than 100 corporate seats for thousands of applicants. Unlike many programs, Royal Caribbean lists a 3.2 GPA as "highly preferred" and requires US work authorization. Externships are short, remote professional experience programs where you finish a real project with a real company. The Beats by Dre Data Analytics Externship and the Amazon Fulfillment Center Operational Strategy Externship build exactly the data analysis and operations evidence a Royal Caribbean application needs. Explore all Externships . What Is a Royal Caribbean Group Internship? A Royal Caribbean Group internship is a paid, 10-week summer placement that puts roughly 80–100 college students into real roles across 10+ departments at the company's South Florida offices, from Technology and Data Analytics & AI to Supply Chain and Maritime Architecture. The program earned Vault's #1 Best Travel & Transportation Internship for 2026 and ranks #2 for Data Analytics and #3 for Overall Inclusion . The company itself holds a 3.8 out of 5 on Glassdoor from over 2,100 reviews, with 67% recommending it. The program operates on a hybrid schedule (in-person Monday through Thursday, remote Fridays) and culminates in a capstone project presented to VP-level leadership. When Do Royal Caribbean Group Internship Applications Open for 2027–2028? Royal Caribbean's intern recruiting follows a documented two-wave pattern: postings go live August through November for early-bird applicants, then a second wave opens January through April. The 2026 cycle's Supply Chain posting carried a December 2, 2025 deadline for a June 1, 2026 start, confirming a roughly 6-month lead. All applications are reviewed on a rolling basis, and live job descriptions warn that positions "may close before the stated closing date." So for summer 2027 you apply starting fall 2026, about 8–10 months before the June 2027 start. There is no second chance once a posting fills. Now · Summer 2026 you're HERE Summer 2027 postings don't exist yet, and even the earliest wave is roughly two months away. This is the proof-building window: what's on your resume when the portal opens decides whether the rolling review ever reaches you. The Beats by Dre Data Analytics Externship and the Amazon Fulfillment Center Operational Strategy Externship are remote, real-company projects that give a fall application finished work to point at. Rolling review means week-one applications meet the most open seats. October 2026 EXPECTED Diversity pathway scholarship deadline expected (historically earlier than general applications). First-round interviews begin: HireVue video screen followed by recruiter and hiring manager rounds. January–April 2027 EXPECTED Second wave of postings. Additional departments open. Offers continue rolling for early applicants from the first wave. Late applicants compete for remaining seats. June 1, 2027 Expected program start. 10 weeks of hybrid work in South Florida through early August. The program ends with a capstone presentation to VP-level leadership, which factors into full-time conversion decisions. Why You Must Apply the Week Applications Open Royal Caribbean's own careers FAQ says applications are "reviewed on a rolling basis and it's in the applicant's best interest to apply early." Live job descriptions add that positions "may close before the stated closing date, you're encouraged to apply as soon as possible." Rolling means the cohort fills while the window is still open, and with only 80–100 corporate seats against thousands of applicants, the math is simple: the longer you wait, the fewer seats remain. Aim to submit within the first 2–3 weeks of a posting going live. Which Royal Caribbean Group Internship Programs Should You Target? Royal Caribbean runs 10+ intern tracks across its South Florida offices, spanning everything from cruising technology to maritime ship design. Which one should you pick? The honest answer is the one whose skills you can already show, because each department interviews against its own job description. Program Focus Duration Key skills Technology IT systems, digital transformation, innovation in cruising 10 weeks CS, Data Science; Python, SQL, Java; agile methodology Data Analytics & AI Data-driven decision-making, ML, business intelligence 10 weeks Python, SQL, R; data visualization; machine learning Finance & Accounting Revenue management, financial analysis, global business operations 10 weeks Excel (pivot tables, VLOOKUP), financial modeling, business analytics Supply Chain & Procurement Procurement, logistics, inventory across a global fleet 10 weeks Demand planning, vendor management, business analytics Marketing & Sales Creative campaigns, brand strategy, strategic partnerships 10 weeks Digital marketing platforms, social media analytics, CRM Maritime Architecture & Design Innovative ship design, blending creativity and engineering 10 weeks Engineering, Architecture, Industrial Design See all tracks on the official intern program page . Other departments include Hospitality / Hotel Operations, Business Operations, Entertainment, and Human Resources. And note: Royal Caribbean also runs a separate shipboard internship track with 200–300 positions annually across the fleet. What Are the Eligibility Requirements? Royal Caribbean publishes the same core requirements across its corporate internship postings: • Enrollment: currently enrolled in a 4-year Bachelor's or Graduate program. Rising seniors are the primary target for corporate roles; MBA and graduate students are eligible for specialized tracks. • Graduation: expected graduation of December 2027 or May 2028 (for the summer 2027 cohort). You must still be enrolled; graduated students aren't eligible. • Work authorization: permanent US work authorization required. Royal Caribbean doesn't sponsor H-1B visas for interns, but CPT and OPT are accepted. • Availability: must be available without interruption for the full 10-week program (early June through early August). Does Royal Caribbean Have a GPA Cutoff? Sort of. Most postings list a minimum GPA of 3.2 as "highly preferred," and some sources cite 3.0 as the floor. But "highly preferred" is a screening preference, not a hard gate. Strong hospitality or service industry experience, relevant coursework, leadership roles, and employee referrals can offset a borderline GPA. That said, with fewer than 100 seats and a sub-5% acceptance rate, higher is always better for competitive departments like Finance and Data Analytics & AI. Royal Caribbean also explicitly allows candidates to apply to multiple internships , so cast a deliberate net across the tracks where your skills are strongest. What Skills Does Royal Caribbean Group Look For, and How Do You Build Them? Across Royal Caribbean's 2026-cycle job descriptions for Supply Chain, Data Analytics & AI, Finance, and other tracks, a clear pattern emerges. Communication shows up in virtually every posting, often specified as "excellent communication skills (oral and written)" with a cross-cultural emphasis that reflects the company's global fleet. Data analysis and technical proficiency vary by department but cluster around Excel, Python, SQL, and visualization tools. And the soft-skill overlap is striking: adaptability, customer service orientation, and collaborative teamwork appear across nearly all tracks, which makes sense for a company that operates floating cities. Skill (from real JDs) JD evidence Externship that builds it Data analysis & visualization (Python, SQL) Data Analytics & AI JD: "Python, SQL, R; data visualization"; Finance track: "data analysis" Beats by Dre Data Analytics Financial modeling & business analysis Finance & Accounting track: "financial modeling," "Excel (pivot tables, VLOOKUP)" Yinan Zhao Investing & Financial Modeling Supply chain & operations analytics Supply Chain JD: "demand planning, vendor management"; Business Operations track Amazon Fulfillment Center Operational Strategy Consumer behavior & market analysis Marketing & Sales track: "brand strategy," "social media analytics," "CRM" Beats by Dre Consumer Behavior & Market Analysis AI & machine learning engineering Data Analytics & AI JD: ML, BI; Technology track: digital transformation Wayfair AI Agent Engineering for Business Intelligence How close is the overlap? The Amazon operations deliverable mirrors the Supply Chain JD's demand-planning language, and the capstone presentation every Externship ends on is the "excellent communication" line item that appears across all 10 Royal Caribbean tracks. What Is the Royal Caribbean Group Application and Interview Process Like? Royal Caribbean's corporate internship pipeline runs 4–6 rounds, and the full process typically takes 2–4 weeks from first contact to offer, though some candidates report up to 2 months: 1. Create a profile at careers.royalcaribbeangroup.com and browse "Students & Recent Grads" postings. Submit your resume, educational background, work history, and availability. Some applications include 2–4 behavioral or situational questions. 2. HireVue on-demand video interview. 3–5 pre-set behavioral and situational questions, recorded asynchronously. This is the initial screening gate for most corporate tracks. 3. Recruiter screen (phone or video, 15–30 minutes) followed by a hiring manager interview (video, 30–60 minutes, STAR-format behavioral questions). Common themes: "Why Royal Caribbean?", customer service scenarios, adaptability, cross-cultural teamwork. 4. Final interview or assessment for select competitive roles: a case study for Finance/Revenue Management, a coding challenge (HackerRank or Codility) for Technology/Data Analytics, or a senior leadership panel. Then: offer, background check, and drug screening. The program concludes with a capstone project presentation to VP-level leadership, which factors into conversion decisions. Rehearse the behavioral rounds with STAR format: our HireVue question guide with a free AI mock tool runs the same time pressure. Three moves, all executable before postings go live in fall 2026. First, apply in the first two weeks of a posting; rolling review plus a "positions close when filled" warning makes timing itself a filter. Second, build evidence in the JD's exact vocabulary. A finished data analytics or operations project answers "tell me about a time you analyzed data" with an artifact instead of an anecdote, and it shows the cross-cultural communication and customer-service orientation Royal Caribbean screens for across all 10 tracks. Third, apply to multiple tracks. Royal Caribbean explicitly says candidates can submit applications to multiple internships, so cast a deliberate net where your skills are strongest. And remember: the capstone presentation to VP-level leadership is how they decide who gets a return offer. Interview like someone auditioning for the full-time seat, because you're. What Other Companies Should You Consider? Royal Caribbean's peer set splits by industry: cruise lines with similar programs, and hospitality giants with earlier or larger calendars. FAQ When do Royal Caribbean internship applications open for summer 2027? Based on the 2026 cycle, expect the first wave of summer 2027 postings in August–November 2026, with a second wave January–April 2027. Royal Caribbean reviews applications on a rolling basis and positions close when filled, so applying within the first few weeks of a posting going live gives you the best chance. Is Royal Caribbean internship recruiting rolling? Yes. The official careers FAQ says applications are "reviewed on a rolling basis" and it's "in the applicant's best interest to apply early." Live job descriptions warn positions "may close before the stated closing date." Earlier applications get priority screening, especially for competitive departments like Finance and Data Analytics. What GPA do you need for a Royal Caribbean internship? Most postings list a minimum GPA of 3.2 as "highly preferred," though some cite 3.0 as the floor. The 3.2 is a screening preference, not an absolute cutoff. Strong hospitality experience, relevant coursework, leadership, and employee referrals can offset a borderline GPA, but higher is always better for competitive departments. What is the Royal Caribbean internship interview process like? After applying online, most candidates complete a HireVue asynchronous video interview with 3–5 behavioral questions. Those who pass advance to a recruiter screen and then a hiring manager interview lasting 30–60 minutes. Technical roles may add coding challenges or case studies. The process typically takes 2–4 weeks from first contact to offer. Do Royal Caribbean interns get return offers? Royal Caribbean describes its internship as "a vital talent pipeline." Based on LinkedIn alumni analysis of 2022–2024 cohorts, approximately 60–70% of strong-performing corporate interns receive full-time Analyst or Associate offers. The program culminates with a capstone presentation to senior leadership, which factors into conversion decisions. What skills does Royal Caribbean look for in interns? Technical skills vary by department: advanced Excel for Finance, Python and SQL for Data Analytics, digital marketing tools for Marketing. Across all tracks, Royal Caribbean emphasizes excellent communication, cross-cultural sensitivity, adaptability, customer service orientation, and collaborative teamwork. Prior hospitality or service industry experience is valued but not required. Are Royal Caribbean internships paid? Yes. All corporate internships are paid at $21–$24 per hour for undergraduate positions, with some Glassdoor reports averaging $33/hr for technical roles. The program runs 40 hours per week in a hybrid format (in-person Monday through Thursday, remote Fridays). Non-local interns may receive a one-time relocation stipend of $1,000–$2,000. Can international students apply for Royal Caribbean internships? Royal Caribbean requires permanent US work authorization and doesn't sponsor H-1B visas for interns. However, CPT and OPT are accepted, so international students with valid CPT or OPT authorization can apply. You must also be currently enrolled in a US 4-year Bachelor's or Graduate program. The window is rolling and the seats fill fast. Spend the runway building proof: a remote Externship turns "interested in hospitality" into a finished project a fall application can point at. body_text: If you're evaluating forest admin alternatives, you're likely hitting one of three friction points: per-user pricing that scales poorly, limited self-hosting flexibility, or customization ceilings that slow your team down. Forest Admin auto-generates admin panels from your database schema and handles CRUD, dashboards, and permissions well - but at roughly US $60 per user per month on its Scale/Pro tier, with no meaningful free plan and SaaS-first deployment, it's not the right tool for every team or budget. This article breaks down six credible alternatives to Forest Admin - Jet Admin, Retool, Appsmith, Budibase, UI Bakery, and AdminJS - across the criteria that actually drive the decision: build speed, data connectivity, extensibility, deployment control, governance, pricing, and maintenance overhead. Each section names strengths, limitations, and the specific team profile each tool fits best, so you can shortcut the evaluation process. The short answer: There's no single replacement that beats Forest Admin on every axis. Budibase and Appsmith are the strongest picks for cost-sensitive or open-source-focused teams. Jet Admin is a great choice for organizations that need broad integrations with enterprise-grade governance and self-hosted deployment. Retool wins on component maturity but at premium cost. UI Bakery stands out for design-focused, security-conscious teams. AdminJS gives maximum control to Node.js developers willing to build from scratch. The right tool depends on your team size, technical capability, compliance requirements, and budget. How to Evaluate Forest Admin Alternatives: Key Criteria Before comparing specific platforms, it helps to define the dimensions that actually separate these tools. Not every criterion matters equally to every team - but skipping any of them leads to surprise costs or migration headaches later. Build speed and ease of setup. How quickly can you connect a data source and have a working admin interface? Tools that auto-generate CRUD views from a database schema (like Forest Admin does) get you to a prototype faster, but may restrict layout flexibility. Visual builders and low-code platforms enable rapid development of admin panels and dashboards, though the trade-off is often less granular control. Data connectivity options. Does the platform connect to your databases (PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB, etc.), REST and GraphQL APIs, SaaS tools (Stripe, Salesforce, HubSpot), and spreadsheets? Open-source platforms often integrate with various APIs and data sources, but verify the specific connectors you need before committing. Extensibility and customization. Can you write custom JavaScript, build custom UI components, or extend logic beyond the drag and drop interface? Some platforms offer pre built components and visual builders; others are code-first. The gap between "demo-ready" and "production-ready" often lives here. Authentication, permissions, and role-based access control. SSO/SAML/SCIM support, fine-grained RBAC down to row and column level, multi-factor authentication, session timeouts. These features protect sensitive data and are non-negotiable for teams in healthcare, finance, or manufacturing. Deployment options. Cloud-hosted SaaS, self-hosted on your own infrastructure, on-premise behind a VPN, or air-gapped for regulated environments. Forest Admin is primarily SaaS; many alternatives offer more deployment flexibility. Governance features. Audit logs, activity history, data residency controls, IP whitelisting, compliance certifications (SOC-2, HIPAA). These aren't checkboxes - the depth and retention of logs, and where data actually lives, determine whether you pass an audit. Pricing model and total cost of ownership. Per-user flat pricing, builder vs. end-user seat types, action-based caps, AI credit metering. Hidden costs (log retention, branding, premium support) inflate TCO beyond the sticker price. Maintenance requirements and technical overhead. Self-hosting means managing upgrades, backups, security patches, and scaling. SaaS offloads that work but reduces control. Teams without DevOps capacity should weigh this heavily. Forest Admin Alternatives: Comparison at a Glance Factor Jet Admin Retool Appsmith Budibase UI Bakery AdminJS Best for Enterprise governance + broad integrations Complex internal tools with large component needs Open-source flexibility on a budget Quick CRUD apps with self-hosting Design-focused teams with security needs Node.js devs wanting full control Free / Open-Source Free tier available Free tier; limited Community edition (open source) Open source (GPLv3), free self-hosted Free tier with limits Fully open source Self-Hosted / On-Premise Yes - VPN, VPC, air-gapped Enterprise tier only Yes Yes (Docker/K8s) Yes Fully self-hosted (you deploy) Pricing Entry Point Contact for current tiers Free; paid plans scale by seat type Free (5 users cloud); Business ~$15/user/mo Free self-hosted; Cloud Pro ~$19/mo Free; Builder seats from ~$25/mo No SaaS cost; you bear infra + dev Key Governance RBAC, SSO/SAML/SCIM, audit logs, 2FA, IP whitelisting Strong enterprise governance RBAC, audit logs; SAML/SCIM in enterprise SSO, RBAC, audit logs in higher tiers SOC-2, audit logs, SSO, advanced RBAC You implement governance manually Key Limitation Verify current pricing; advanced customization learning curve Cost escalates; self-hosting restricted Less polish; enterprise features gated Action caps; fewer integrations Per-builder cost high; AI credits separate Requires significant dev effort Key takeaway: If budget and open-source freedom are priorities, Appsmith and Budibase lead. If enterprise security, deployment control, and broad data connectivity matter most, Jet Admin and UI Bakery are the strongest contenders. Retool is the most mature platform but the most expensive at scale. Jet Admin Best for: Teams that need to build internal tools across many data sources with enterprise-grade governance and flexible deployment - especially organizations in regulated industries requiring self-hosted or on-premise setups. Jet Admin enables the building of tools without extensive coding. It connects to existing databases, APIs, spreadsheets, and SaaS tools, then generates the interface and application logic so you can deploy apps to users quickly. JetAdmin allows a drag-and-drop interface for internal tools and apps, enabling both rapid prototyping and production-grade business applications. Key strengths: Extensive data connectivity. Jet Admin's verified integrations page lists connectors for PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB, Firestore, Supabase, BigQuery, Snowflake, Databricks, Microsoft SQL, MariaDB, Oracle, SQLite, CockroachDB, Amazon Athena, ClickHouse, AlloyDB, and more. SaaS integrations include Stripe, HubSpot, Salesforce, Slack, Shopify, Zendesk, Intercom, QuickBooks, and others. AI providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, DeepSeek) and storage services (AWS S3, Azure Blob, Google Cloud Storage) are also supported. Enterprise governance. Role-based access control down to rows, columns, and actions. SSO/SAML/SCIM support, audit logs, 2FA, IP whitelisting, branded/custom-domain experiences, auto-logout, and incident recovery/backups. Deployment flexibility. Supports cloud, self-hosted, on-premise, and deployment behind VPN or VPC - critical for teams that need to protect data sovereignty or meet air-gapped compliance requirements. Customization. Visual builder for drag-and-drop development, plus custom SQL, API requests, custom JavaScript, and a JS SDK for building custom UI components (React/Vue/Angular). Data blending across various data sources is supported. Limitations: Jet Admin's public pricing tiers are not clearly published as of mid-2026 - teams should contact sales for current rates. For organizations with many users, per-seat cost may be significant, as is typical in this category. Advanced customization features carry a steeper learning curve than simpler visual builders. Managing self-hosted infrastructure requires DevOps investment. How it compares to Forest Admin: Both tools auto-generate interfaces from your data schema, which accelerates setup for standard CRUD panels. Jet Admin offers a broader connector catalog and more deployment options (including on-premise and air-gapped), whereas Forest Admin's deployment is primarily SaaS with enterprise-only customization. Jet Admin's governance features (row/column-level RBAC, IP whitelisting, audit logs) are available without necessarily jumping to a custom enterprise contract. Retool Best for: Technical teams building complex, highly customized internal tools who need a mature platform with an extensive component library and are willing to pay a premium. Retool offers a rich set of pre-built components for app building - tables, forms, charts, maps, modals, and more - along with deep integrations, workflow automation, and portal/external user support. Retool provides pre-built components for building internal tools that cover most standard admin use cases without frontend development from scratch. Key strengths: Component maturity. One of the largest libraries of pre built components for building apps, dashboards, and admin interfaces. Strong support for custom JavaScript and SQL. Integrations. Retool allows integration with various databases and APIs, including PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB, REST, GraphQL, Stripe, Salesforce, and many others. Governance. Enterprise tier includes advanced features: SSO/SAML, granular permissions, audit logs, version control, and workflow automation. Strong for organizations that need detailed access control. Limitations: Cost escalation. Retool prices differ by seat types - builders, internal users, and external users - which creates complexity and unpredictability. Builders cost significantly more, and external user gating adds up. At scale, Retool is one of the most expensive options in this comparison. Self-hosting restricted. Retool has moved self-hosting into enterprise-only plans , eliminating affordable self-hosted options for smaller teams. This is a dealbreaker for teams that need deployment control without an enterprise contract. Learning curve. While powerful, Retool is less intuitive for non technical users than simpler visual builders like Budibase or UI Bakery. How it compares to Forest Admin: Both are polished, enterprise-capable platforms. Retool gives more flexibility in building custom admin panels and complex workflows, but at higher cost. Forest Admin's schema-first approach generates panels faster for standard CRUD; Retool requires more manual mapping but offers deeper customization. Neither is ideal for budget-constrained teams. Appsmith Best for: Developer teams wanting open-source flexibility with a low-code approach, especially those who want to self-host without licensing fees. Appsmith is an open-source low-code platform for internal tools. Its community edition is free and self-hostable, making it one of the most accessible alternatives to Forest Admin for teams that prioritize control and cost. Key strengths: Open-source core. Appsmith is an open-source low-code platform for internal tools, with a thriving community and transparent development. Appsmith allows building internal tools with a low-code approach that suits developers comfortable with JavaScript customization. Pricing simplicity. Appsmith's Business plan is $15/user/month ; its Enterprise plan is $2,500/month for 100 users. The free cloud plan supports up to five users. All users are charged the same rate regardless of role - no builder vs. end-user seat confusion. Self-hosting. Full support for self-hosted deployment, enabling teams to run Appsmith on their own infrastructure without licensing cost (community edition). Workflows and version control. Business and Enterprise plans include workflows, reusable packages, Git version control, unlimited workspaces, and customizable roles. Limitations: Enterprise features like SAML/OIDC/SCIM, private embedding, and air-gapped setups are only available on the Enterprise plan. UI polish and advanced features lag behind Retool and Forest Admin in some areas - debugging complex layouts or data flows can require more manual work. The free tier caps at five users on cloud, with limited workspaces and versioning, so scaling beyond a small team means paying. How it compares to Forest Admin: Appsmith is substantially cheaper, especially for teams with many users. Forest Admin auto-generates panels from your schema; Appsmith requires more manual data-source binding and UI layout work. For teams that value open-source transparency and want to avoid vendor lock-in, Appsmith is a strong pick. For teams that want instant CRUD generation and don't worry about per-seat cost, Forest Admin is faster to start. Budibase Best for: Small to medium teams that need to create CRUD applications quickly, with the option to self-host for free. Budibase is an open-source platform for creating internal tools. It offers excellent automatic CRUD generation for business applications and is designed for both technical and non-technical users, making it accessible across organizations without deep frontend development expertise. Key strengths: Generous free tier. Budibase offers a free self-hosted plan under GPLv3 with unlimited users - one of the most cost-efficient ways to get started building apps. Cloud Pro starts at $19/month; Business at approximately $299/month. Built-in database and CRUD. Budibase excels at rapidly creating CRUD applications. Its built-in database (BudibaseDB) lets you start building without connecting an external data source, and it supports Docker and Kubernetes deployments for self-hosting. Accessible to mixed teams. Budibase supports both non-technical and experienced users, enabling teams to build internal tools without requiring every contributor to write code. Budibase is designed for both non-technical and experienced users. Governance (higher tiers). SSO, RBAC with user groups, enforced SSO, audit logs (retention grows with tier), and Active Directory/SCIM in the Enterprise plan. Limitations: Automated actions (workflows) are capped per plan - teams with heavy automation needs will hit limits on lower tiers. The integration ecosystem is smaller than Retool's or Jet Admin's. Fewer SaaS connectors out of the box means more custom API work for some use cases. UI polish and token management may feel less refined than more mature platforms; premium support and advanced features (custom branding, 365-day log retention) require Enterprise. How it compares to Forest Admin: Budibase's free self-hosted option is its biggest advantage for cost-sensitive teams. Forest Admin is faster for initial CRUD generation from an existing schema, but Budibase's built-in database and visual builder close that gap for many use cases. Forest Admin's governance features are more mature in enterprise tiers, but Budibase offers similar capabilities at a fraction of the cost - especially for teams comfortable with self-hosting. UI Bakery Best for: Design-focused teams that prioritize polished user interfaces, need SOC-2 compliance, and want both cloud and self-hosted deployment options. UI Bakery offers a drag-and-drop interface for building admin panels with a focus on visual design quality and security. It supports AI-powered app generation, custom components, environment separation (dev/staging/prod), and release history - making it a scalable solution for teams building apps for internal or external users. Key strengths: Visual design and templates. UI Bakery's drag and drop interface and template library make it efficient for teams that want polished admin panels without extensive frontend development. AI-driven app generation accelerates prototyping. Security and compliance. UI Bakery is SOC-2 certified , supporting audit logs, advanced RBAC (Admin, Editor, custom roles), SSO (Okta, Azure AD, SAML, OIDC), 2FA/MFA, and self-hosted deployments for HIPAA or PCI configurations. Deployment flexibility. Cloud and self-hosted options, including air-gapped configurations for regulated environments. Pricing. Free plan allows unlimited apps and data source connections. Developer seats start at approximately $25–$40/month depending on plan. Limitations: Developer seat-based pricing means costs rise quickly as you add builders. The free plan lacks audit logs and advanced permissions. White-labelling, premium support, and some advanced features are only available in higher tiers. AI usage often involves separate credits or limitations, which can be a hidden cost driver. How it compares to Forest Admin: UI Bakery offers stronger visual design tools and more deployment flexibility than Forest Admin, plus SOC-2 certification on its core platform. Forest Admin's schema-first auto-generation is faster for standard CRUD, but UI Bakery provides more control over the look and feel of custom admin panels. For teams in healthcare, finance, or other regulated industries, UI Bakery's self-hosted and compliance features are a meaningful advantage. AdminJS Best for: Node.js developers who want full control over their admin interface, are comfortable writing code, and want to avoid SaaS licensing costs entirely. AdminJS is an open-source admin panel for Node.js applications. You embed it directly into your Express, NestJS, or other Node.js frameworks, giving you complete control over deployment, logic, layout, and customization. Open-source frameworks provide customizability for admin panels - and AdminJS exemplifies this approach. Key strengths: Total control. Because AdminJS is code-first, you control every aspect: UI, business logic, permissions, deployment. It integrates into your existing Node.js project, so there's no separate platform to manage. No SaaS cost. AdminJS is fully open source with no per-seat licensing. Your cost is infrastructure and development time. Deployment freedom. Self-host anywhere - on-premise, in a VPC, air-gapped, or on any cloud provider. No vendor dependency for deployment or uptime. Limitations: Significant development effort. There's no visual builder or drag and drop interface. Defining resources, permissions, custom actions, and audit logs requires JavaScript code. Non technical users cannot build or modify panels without developer support. Maintenance burden. You're responsible for updates, compatibility with underlying frameworks, security patches, and feature development. Custom components and plugins need ongoing maintenance. No built-in governance. RBAC, audit logs, SSO, and compliance features must be implemented or integrated manually. There are community plugins, but nothing comparable to the out-of-the-box governance in SaaS tools. How it compares to Forest Admin: AdminJS is the opposite end of the spectrum from Forest Admin's managed SaaS approach. Forest Admin gives you a working panel in minutes; AdminJS gives you unlimited flexibility but requires you to build from scratch. For Node.js teams with strong development capacity who need to embed admin functionality inside an existing application, AdminJS is the right tool. For teams that want to launch quickly with minimal code, it's not. Which Forest Admin Alternative Should You Choose? The best admin alternative depends on your team's profile, not a universal ranking. Here's how to match: Choose Jet Admin if you need enterprise governance (SSO/SAML/SCIM, row-level RBAC, audit logs) with the broadest set of data source integrations and the option to deploy on-premise or behind a VPN. It's a great choice for mid-to-large organizations in regulated industries that want to build internal tools quickly without sacrificing security or deployment control. Choose Retool if you have technical teams, budget for premium features, and need the most mature component library and workflow automation. Be prepared for cost escalation with many builder seats, and note that self-hosting is now enterprise-only. Choose Appsmith if you want open-source flexibility, predictable per-user pricing, and the ability to self-host without licensing fees. Best for developer-led teams comfortable with JavaScript who want to avoid vendor lock-in. Choose Budibase if you need quick CRUD app setup with a generous free self-hosted tier. Ideal for startups and small-to-medium businesses that want to build internal tools efficiently without a large budget, especially when the team includes both technical and non-technical users. Choose UI Bakery if design quality and compliance are top priorities. Its SOC-2 certification, intuitive visual builder, and self-hosted deployment make it well-suited for teams in healthcare, finance, or any sector where security and polished user experiences matter. Choose AdminJS if you're a Node.js development team that wants complete control, no SaaS dependency, and is willing to invest engineering time in exchange for maximum customization and zero licensing cost. By team size and skill: Team Profile Top Pick Runner-Up Small startup, 2–5 developers, low budget Budibase (free self-hosted) Appsmith (free community edition) Mid-sized company, 50–200 users, needs governance Jet Admin UI Bakery Highly regulated enterprise (finance, healthcare) Jet Admin or UI Bakery (self-hosted) AdminJS (full control) Non-technical or citizen developer teams Budibase UI Bakery Teams needing external-facing apps or portals Retool Jet Admin General internal tool platforms support custom applications and dashboards - but the specifics of your deployment, compliance, and team composition should drive the final decision. Migration and Selection Checklist Switching from Forest Admin (or any admin panel builder) involves more than feature comparison. Use this checklist to avoid common migration pitfalls: Data and Schema Does the new tool auto-sync when your database schema evolves, or will you need to manually update UI mappings after every migration or schema change? Can you connect to all your current data sources - databases, APIs, SaaS tools - without building custom connectors? Integration Lift List all existing dashboards, workflows, custom actions, and integrations in your current Forest Admin setup. Which must be rebuilt? Which have direct equivalents in the new platform? User and Seat Mapping Count how many users are builders, how many are end users or viewers. Map these against the new tool's seat types. Mismatches here cause the biggest cost surprises - for example, Budibase distinguishes "creator" vs. "end-user" seats, while Appsmith charges all users the same rate. Deployment and Infrastructure If self-hosting, assess your infrastructure: servers, networking, backup, monitoring, and compliance (data residency, encryption at rest and in transit). For air-gapped or on-premise requirements, verify the tool's support explicitly - not all "self-hosted" options are truly air-gappable. Security and Governance Checklist: SSO/SAML/SCIM, 2FA/MFA, row/column/action-level permissions, audit logs with retention policies, IP whitelisting, encrypted channels, disaster recovery (backups/version rollback), incident response tools. Total Cost of Ownership Include: subscription/licensing fees + infrastructure cost for hosting + development effort + staff for maintenance + cost of external users + cost for upgrading tiers + cost for features like branding, AI usage, and extended log retention. Timeline and Resource Planning Estimate months, not weeks, for medium-sized app migrations. Plan for overlap so tools can be phased rather than cut over immediately. Budget for retraining, integration testing, and permission audits. Frequently Asked Questions Can I migrate my existing Forest Admin setup to these alternatives? Yes, but expect to rebuild rather than export-and-import. Forest Admin's schema-first approach means your data model carries over, but dashboards, custom actions, workflows, and permissions will need to be recreated in the new tool. Plan for a phased migration with parallel operation during the transition. Which alternatives offer the best value for small development teams? Budibase and Appsmith are the strongest options for small teams. Budibase's free self-hosted tier supports unlimited users at no licensing cost. Appsmith's free cloud plan covers up to five users, and its Business plan is $15/user/month - significantly cheaper than Forest Admin's ~$60/user/month. How do these platforms compare for enterprise security and compliance? Jet Admin and UI Bakery offer the deepest out-of-the-box governance: SSO/SAML/SCIM, audit logs, IP whitelisting, self-hosted and on-premise deployment, and (for UI Bakery) SOC-2 certification. Retool's enterprise tier is also strong but expensive and SaaS-dependent for most customers. AdminJS gives total control, but you build every governance feature yourself. What's the typical setup time for each Forest Admin alternative? For standard CRUD admin panels over an existing database, tools like Jet Admin, Budibase, and Retool can produce a working prototype within hours. Appsmith and UI Bakery require slightly more manual setup but are still fast for basic use cases. AdminJS requires the most development time - days to weeks depending on complexity - because everything is built in code. Are there other notable admin panel builders worth considering? Yes. Directus automatically generates admin interfaces and supports various databases - it's considered a close replacement for Forest Admin by some teams. NocoBase generates CRUD operations from a database schema. ToolJet is an open-source low-code platform for dashboard creation and facilitates the development of complex internal tools. DronaHQ offers unlimited cross-platform apps with native UI features and enables building internal tools without CSS rules or extensive coding. Refine is a headless React framework for building data-intensive internal tools, suited for developers looking for maintainable React applications. Active Admin automatically generates backend interfaces for Ruby on Rails, Django Admin is a built-in admin interface for Django projects, and Laravel Nova is a code-first admin panel for Laravel users. WeWeb provides a visual builder to create admin panels. Glide is favored for rapidly generating apps from spreadsheets. Five charges US $29.99 per application per month for 10 users and can instantly generate admin panels from any data source. Boost.space is recognized for integrating data management with CRM capabilities. Admin panel builders help create internal CRUD interfaces over existing databases - the right choice depends on your stack, team, and requirements. Is an open-source alternative always cheaper than Forest Admin? Not necessarily. Open-source platforms allow extensive customization for internal tools, but self-hosting brings infrastructure, maintenance, and staffing costs. A free Budibase or Appsmith deployment still requires server provisioning, backup management, security patching, and upgrade planning. Calculate your total cost of ownership - not just the license fee - before assuming open source is cheaper. Ready to evaluate whether Jet Admin fits your team's requirements? body_text: 📍 Austin, TX 🔗 hotplate.com/tiamannfrenchbakery Lucie didn’t set out to go viral, but a simple post on Instagram Threads did just that. A month later, she sold almost 700 pastries and grossed over $2k on a single weekly drop . She’s been hustling to keep up with demand and hand laminating each and every pastry from her apartment kitchen ever since. How it started “I just put that I make kouign-amann in Austin and I’m from the region that this pastry is from,” she says. The post picked up hundreds of likes. “People kept commenting that they were so happy to have found me.” Things blew up even more a few weeks later when an Austin-based food account, @austinfoodadventures, shared Lucie’s story, exposing her to a much larger local audience. Ti Amann’s Hotplate subscriber list tripled over the next few weeks. She was selling out every drop, hustling to keep up with demand while ensuring each pastry that came out of her apartment kitchen met her quality standards: buttery, flakey, and perfectly carmelized. She sold almost 700 pastries and grossed more than $2,000 in her first April drop . “I didn’t expect it at all,” Lucie told us. Subscribers to Ti Amann’s Hotplate storefront From bakery employee to running her own Lucie’s baking journey began in France when she was just 15 years old. She completed an apprenticeship as a pastry chef and worked in local bakeries before moving to the United States. Wanting to share both her passion for baking and a taste of home is what inspired her to start making kouign-amann out of her apartment. Before she officially started Ti Amann, Lucie was working full-time for another bakery. As demand for her side hustle grew, it became impossible to do both. “I quickly realized I couldn’t keep up with my job and doing the kouign-amann at the same time. I had to quit.” Now, Ti Amann is her full-time focus. She runs the entire operation from her apartment kitchen, producing hundreds of pastries each week. What her business looks like today Lucie’s prep schedule begins three days before pickups. On Wednesday, she makes her butter sheets and dough, shapes the pastries on Thursday, makes more dough Thursday night, and bakes everything off fresh Saturday and Sunday mornings ahead of pickups. She produces 500 to 700 pastries in a single weekend, all from her apartment kitchen. Somehow, she’s still laminating by hand and hasn’t bought a sheeter yet! Thankfully, Lucie’s husband helps set up boxes, moves dough to the fridge after shaping, and attends to customers at pop-ups. For now, she plans to keep the business home-based. “It’s very convenient to be able to work from home. Maybe in the future, if I have so much demand, I could move to a kitchen.” Discovering Hotplate When Lucie first decided to start her microbakery, she didn’t even know this kind of business was possible. “I didn't even know that it was a thing that I could do…I just found it randomly online, I saw people that were doing it.” Determined to not have to create her own website, she went searching for alternatives. “I found Hotplate and everyone was saying it was the best website to use because it was really convenient.” A lesson that shaped her approach Q: What’s a piece of advice about running a baking business that changed how you work? A: Plan ahead! “When I started I was not really planning everything ahead and I was rushing. I quickly realized I needed to plan ahead because it was not sustainable to be doing everything last minute.” More than just pastries Lucie’s business is still evolving, but she’s clear on what she enjoys. She’s focused on maintaining what’s working: a flexible, home-based setup that allows her to keep up with demand without overextending or overinvesting. She’s experimenting with new flavors, including a strawberry vanilla kouign-amann, and continuing to refine her processes week by week. “I really like where I’m at right now,” she says. To other entrepreneurs, Lucie’s story is a reminder to make that post, send the message, print the flyer. Something might catch on when you least expect it. And when it does, the challenge becomes keeping up while building something sustainable and enjoyable. For Lucie, that means staying organized, planning ahead, and continuing to do what got her here in the first place: making incredible pastries, one fold at a time.

title: Living in Trinity Park, Durham, NC
summary: Thinking about living in Trinity Park, Durham, NC? Learn what makes this historic neighborhood so desirable, why buyers pay a premium for walkability, how it compares to Duke Park, and whether Trinity Park is the right fit for your lifestyle.
body_text: Living in Trinity Park , Durham, NC: Is the Walkability Worth the Price? If you're searching for the most walkable neighborhood in Durham, North Carolina, one name almost always rises to the top: Trinity Park . With its century-old homes, towering tree canopy, deep front porches, and unbeatable location between Duke University's East Campus and downtown Durham, Trinity Park has become one of the city's most coveted places to live. But here's something many buyers don't realize... The premium you pay for Trinity Park isn't necessarily a higher purchase price. It's often less house for the same money . That may sound surprising, but it's one of the most important things to understand before buying in this historic neighborhood. Where Is Trinity Park? Trinity Park sits just north of downtown Durham between Duke University's East Campus and Club Boulevard, making it one of the most walkable neighborhoods in the Triangle. Residents can easily walk to: Downtown Durham restaurants Breweries and coffee shops Duke East Campus Parks Entertainment Local events For buyers who genuinely enjoy walking to dinner or meeting friends downtown, few neighborhoods compare. A Neighborhood Full of History Established in the early 1900s, Trinity Park is one of Durham's original residential neighborhoods. Its streets are lined with mature hardwood trees and homes built between approximately 1900 and 1940. Instead of cookie-cutter construction, you'll find: Craftsman homes Colonial Revival architecture Large front porches Original hardwood floors Built-in bookcases Historic details that simply aren't found in newer construction That charm is a major reason buyers fall in love with Trinity Park. Of course, historic homes also come with historic maintenance. Older plumbing, original windows, aging electrical systems, and ongoing upkeep are all part of owning a home with over a century of character. The Trinity Park Premium Many buyers assume Trinity Park is dramatically more expensive than nearby neighborhoods. That's only partly true. Recent market data shows the median home price in Trinity Park is very similar to neighboring Duke Park. The difference isn't what buyers spend. It's what they receive. Because homes in Trinity Park sell for significantly more per square foot , buyers typically purchase a smaller home on a smaller lot for roughly the same overall price. In other words: You're paying a premium for location and walkability—not additional square footage. For many buyers, that's an excellent investment. For others, it may not be. What You're Really Paying For If the homes aren't larger, where does your money go? Walkability Trinity Park offers something incredibly rare in the Triangle. Residents can actually leave their homes on foot and enjoy downtown Durham without driving. Restaurants. Coffee shops. Breweries. Festivals. Duke University. They're all nearby. If you regularly take advantage of that lifestyle, the premium can absolutely be worth it. Historic Character No new subdivision can replicate the feeling of Trinity Park. The mature landscaping, welcoming front porches, and timeless architecture create an atmosphere that's difficult to duplicate. Many buyers specifically seek neighborhoods with history rather than brand-new construction. Community Because so many residents intentionally choose Trinity Park, the neighborhood has developed a strong sense of community. It's common to see neighbors chatting from their front porches, walking their dogs beneath the tree canopy, or strolling downtown together. Is Trinity Park Right for Everyone? Not necessarily. One of the biggest decisions buyers face is whether they'll actually use the walkability they're paying for. Many first-time buyers picture themselves walking downtown every weekend. Life, however, changes. Families grow. Children arrive. Yards suddenly become more important than sidewalks. Some buyers eventually realize they need more house, more outdoor space, and a different lifestyle. Others remain in Trinity Park for decades because it's exactly what they wanted all along. Neither choice is wrong. The key is understanding which lifestyle fits your future—not just your present. Trinity Park vs. Duke Park One of the most interesting comparisons in Durham is Trinity Park versus neighboring Duke Park. The two communities sit just a few blocks apart and share many of the same advantages: Historic homes Mature trees Excellent location Character-filled architecture Yet buyers often receive: More square footage Larger lots Lower price per square foot in Duke Park. For buyers who drive everywhere anyway, Duke Park can represent exceptional value. For buyers who truly prioritize walking downtown, Trinity Park may still be worth every penny. Important Considerations Before Buying Because Trinity Park is a historic neighborhood, buyers should carefully investigate individual properties. Some homes may include: Historic preservation easements Owner-occupancy requirements Restrictions related to Duke University properties These conditions don't apply to every home, but they can affect future renovations or how the property may be used. Working with an experienced local Realtor is especially valuable in neighborhoods like Trinity Park, where no two homes are exactly alike. Who Should Consider Trinity Park? Trinity Park is an excellent fit for buyers who: Love historic architecture Want to walk to downtown Durham Work at Duke University or Duke Health Appreciate mature neighborhoods Prefer charm over square footage You may want to consider other nearby neighborhoods if your priorities include: Larger yards More living space Lower maintenance Maximum value per square foot Final Thoughts Trinity Park remains one of Durham's most iconic neighborhoods for good reason. Its combination of history, location, walkability, and architectural character creates a lifestyle that's difficult to find elsewhere in the Triangle. The real question isn't whether Trinity Park is worth the premium. It's whether you'll actually use what you're paying for . If your ideal weekend includes walking to coffee, dinner, or a Durham Bulls game beneath a canopy of mature trees, Trinity Park could be exactly what you're looking for. If your priorities lean toward extra space, a larger yard, or room for a growing family, there are excellent nearby neighborhoods that may offer a better long-term fit. At Spotlight Realty, we help buyers compare Durham neighborhoods every day, making sure they choose the community that fits not only their budget, but the lifestyle they'll enjoy for years to come. title: What are the symptoms and signs of stroke?
summary: Learn how to spot the signs of stroke using the B.E. F.A.S.T. acronym.
body_text: What are the symptoms and signs of stroke? In order to know how to treat stroke, we must first understand what exactly a stroke is. Stroke occurs when blood flow is either blocked (ischemic stroke) or an artery bursts (hemorrhagic stroke). When this happens, the brain doesn’t get the blood it needs to function properly. Depending on the severity of the stroke and the area of the brain affected, loss of brain function or death may occur. Motor function, speech and memory are examples of bodily functions that may be impacted. Unfortunately, one in four people over the age of 25 will experience a stroke in their lifetime.1 Given this alarming statistic, it's crucial for everyone to recognize the signs of a stroke and learn how to reduce their risk. “Recognizing the signs and symptoms of a stroke is the first critical step in ensuring patients receive the urgent care they need” said Jim Marucci, President of Stryker's Neurovascular division. “Doctors, nurses, and technicians perform life-saving work, but their efforts can only begin once a stroke is identified. By spreading awareness, we hope to empower more people to act quickly, bridging the gap between the onset of a stroke and the life-saving treatment that follows. Together, we can ensure more patients have a chance at recovery and a brighter future.” Find more resources on stroke awareness and the risk factors of stroke . Spot the signs of stroke and B.E. F.A.S.T B alance Loss of balance, difficulty walking, dizziness, or lack of coordination2 Observe if the person is having trouble staying balanced. If you notice this symptom, check for additional signs. E yes Sudden trouble seeing in one or both eyes.2 If the person experiencing changes in their vision, check for additional symptoms of stroke. F ace Facial drooping and weakness2 Look at the person’s face. Is one side of their face drooping or are they unable to move their lips up and down? If so, check for additional signs. A rms Arm weakness2 A stroke can cause muscle weakness and numbness on one or both sides of the body. Check to see if the person’s arm is lying limp to their side. If so, check for additional symptoms of stroke. S peech Speech difficulty2 If someone is slurring their words and you’re having a hard time understanding them, it’s time to call for help. T ime Time to call emergency medical services if you see these signs of stroke.2 Speed of care matters when it comes to stroke. If you notice someone exhibiting the symptoms above, call emergency services immediately. Ischemic strokes block the flow of blood and as a result, oxygen moving to and from the brain. Fast treatment can lessen the brain damage that stroke can cause.2 This is why it’s so important to B.E. F.A.S.T. Stroke is treatable Stroke generally happens suddenly, and medical care needs to be administered as quickly as possible. The best course of treatment depends on the type of stroke, the patient’s age, the severity of the stroke and other risk factors. title: Upland Software Publishes CEO Letter Outlining Strategic Priorities

body_text: View All News Upland Software Publishes CEO Letter Outlining Strategic Priorities 07/28/2026 AUSTIN, Texas--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Upland Software, Inc. (Nasdaq: UPLD) (“Upland” or the “Company”), a provider of enterprise intelligence that turns knowledge, content, and data into actionable AI-powered outcomes, today issued a letter to shareholders from President and Chief Executive Officer Sean Nathaniel. Under new leadership, Upland is focusing investment on near-term, AI-powered growth opportunities where it sees clear AI tailwinds and competitive advantage, specifically in its knowledge and content automation solutions. The Company is simultaneously pursuing sharper capital allocation across the Company, driving greater efficiency to support investment behind those growth opportunities while also strengthening cash flow generation and reducing debt. “We believe we have an advantage most AI entrants spend years trying to build, an installed base of more than 1,100 enterprise customers who trust us to power their AI journey rather than be displaced by it,” said Nathaniel. “That AI tailwind is real for Upland today, not a future promise; we believe our knowledge and content automation solutions, in particular, are critical to enabling enterprise AI journeys. We’re seeing this as we draw upon our years of domain expertise to both expand within existing customers and onboard new customers in the specific vertical segments where we believe we have proven differentiation and right to win.” “Beyond where we are investing, we are just as disciplined about where we are not,” said Nathaniel. “Across the rest of the business, we are driving efficiency to fund that growth, expand margins, and generate the free cash flow needed to support deleveraging and long-term shareholder value creation.” The full letter is available on the Company’s investor relations website at https://investor.uplandsoftware.com/ . The Company expects to report full second quarter results consistent with previously issued guidance ranges, along with an updated outlook for the third quarter and full year, by mid-August 2026. title: Concorde International Group Secures SG$11.6 Million (Approx. US$9.0 Million) in New Multi-Year Recurring Revenue Contracts
body_text: Singapore, June 17, 2025 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Concorde International Group Ltd. (NASDAQ: CIGL) (“Concorde” or the “Company”), an integrated security services provider that combines physical manpower and innovative technology to deliver effective security solutions, today announced that it has secured a total of SG$11,621,370 (approximately US$9,040,472) in new contracts from January through May 2025. The contracts include engagements with new clients as well as expanded agreements with existing customers across newly secured sites. Majority of the contracts represent multi-year recurring revenue, to be recognized over the 2025–2029 period. The wins include four contracts awarded via public tenders, with two coming from Singapore government-related organizations. These contracts span a variety of sites, including schools, factories, and banks, reflecting Concorde’s robust capability in delivering tailored security solutions to critical infrastructure. By comparison, Concorde signed SG$10,915,868 (approximately US$8,492,916) in similar recurring contracts for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2024. The Company’s continued growth reinforces its position as a leading provider of integrated security services in Singapore—one of Asia’s most advanced and competitive security markets. Concorde has gained significant recognition for its disruptive innovation in the integrated monitoring of properties, assets, and building systems, ensuring round-the-clock surveillance and operational efficiency. This is made possible through its proprietary suite of intelligent security solutions known as “I-Guarding Services.” Swee (Alan) Kheng Chua, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Concorde, commented, “We’re only halfway through the year, and we’ve already surpassed the total value of new contracts signed in all of 2024. These new contracts validate the market’s confidence in our solutions and position us for continued growth as we expand our footprint in both the public and private sectors. Singapore remains one of the most sophisticated and competitive security markets in Asia, and our continued momentum reinforces Concorde’s leadership in delivering reliable, technology-driven security and facilities management solutions to a diverse client base.” About Concorde International Group Ltd Concorde International Group Limited (Nasdaq: CIGL) is a Singapore-based company specializing in integrated security solutions and facilities management services. Established in 1997, the Company is recognized for its bold and disruptive innovation with its integrated monitoring of properties, assets and building service systems under 24/7 surveillance, ensuring complete security and business efficiency. This is done through a suite of smart security solutions called “I-Guarding Solutions”. The first of these solutions is its patented I-Man Facility Sprinter (“IFS”) – a revolutionary mobile vehicular platform providing security and facility maintenance services. title: Why Legacy CIP Configuration Monitoring Platforms Are Reaching A Breaking Point
summary: Explore the importance of CIP Configuration Monitoring Platforms for compliance automation and audit readiness in electric utilities.
body_text: Energy 07-09-2026 Why Legacy CIP Configuration Monitoring Platforms Are Reaching A Breaking Point Facebook Twitter LinkedIn Email Estimated reading time: 7 minutes Key Takeaways Parsons helps utilities move beyond manual audit preparation by turning configuration visibility into actionable, audit-ready compliance workflows. SigmaFlow and SigmaFlow Beacon connect monitoring, reviews, attestations, exceptions, and evidence management in one streamlined environment. With Parsons, utilities can reduce disconnected reporting, preserve key compliance decisions, and strengthen NERC CIP audit readiness at scale. Moving From Visibility To Audit-Ready Action Legacy compliance and configuration monitoring platforms still do useful work. However, visibility alone does not create audit-ready action. In many NERC CIP environments, the real bottleneck is no longer detection. It is the manual effort teams spend collecting evidence, coordinating reviews, and keeping the process moving. That is why the conversation has shifted from configuration visibility to compliance automation, workflow orchestration, and audit readiness at scale. Based on a recent conversation with electric utilities, we see clear signs that legacy models are being pushed too far. More importantly, we see why solutions like SigmaFlow are becoming essential for teams that need to move from visibility to action. Manual Audit Work Does Not Scale One team described a biweekly process that required 18 manual reports, extra data pulls from other systems, and a 1,000-page audit package. At that point, you do not have true automation. Instead, you have a reporting ritual that adds overhead, increases error risk, and fails to scale. The issue was not just the volume of output. The process had also become fragmented. The team exported reports, pulled supporting data from other systems, and stitched everything together manually to answer audit questions. That kind of process can survive for a while. However, it creates a constant dependency on extra effort for every reporting cycle. SigmaFlow Helps Reduce Manual Audit Burden SigmaFlow helps utilities reduce that burden by connecting compliance activities, evidence collection, reviews, and approvals in one workflow-driven environment. Rather than relying on disconnected reports and manual coordination, teams can use SigmaFlow to keep the audit process moving with clearer ownership and better traceability. That matters because audit readiness is not just about having the right data. It is also about proving what happened, who reviewed it, what decision was made, and where the evidence lives. Workflow Gaps Create Compliance Bottlenecks Legacy platforms can report changes, but they often stop before the next step begins. Reviews, attestations, and exception handling still happen manually. As a result, teams need systems that pair each issue with the right next step, useful context, and clear ownership. That gap matters because compliance work does not end when a change appears. Someone still has to decide whether the change was expected, route it for review, document the reasoning, and preserve the outcome for later. More advanced platforms go further by embedding control-based workflow actions. For example, SigmaFlow can help teams guide reviews, manage attestations, and support exception handling with more structure. When those steps live in email, spreadsheets, or team memory, teams lose time and consistency. As audit pressure grows, that lack of structure becomes harder to manage. Modern Environments Need Flexible Automation Modern environments rely on APIs, dynamic assets, and distributed data sources. Older configuration collection models do not always fit that reality. When integrations are rigid or difficult to maintain, automation stalls before it starts. Electric utilities also described the challenge of getting data into a usable form. The issue was not simply whether integrations existed. Instead, the real question was whether teams could onboard new sources without a long, brittle effort every time the environment changed. Over time, teams often rely on adjacent tools or command line utilities to move, transform, or extract data from their primary configuration management platform. Those workarounds can extend functionality. However, they also add complexity and overhead. As a result, a workflow that should feel seamless becomes a multi-step process spread across systems. SigmaFlow Beacon Connects Monitoring With Action SigmaFlow Beacon helps extend SigmaFlow’s value by supporting configuration monitoring alongside workflow-driven compliance operations. Together, SigmaFlow and SigmaFlow Beacon help utilities connect monitoring, evidence management, and execution in one environment. That connection is important because teams do not just need to know that something changed. They also need a reliable way to review the change, assign ownership, document the decision, and preserve the outcome for future audits. Data Needs Context To Support Decisions Configuration change detection alone is no longer enough. Teams need current, decision-ready information and guided workflows that reduce their dependence on tribal knowledge. As compliance complexity increases, the cost of manual interpretation keeps rising. Another pain point was how much interpretation depended on a few experienced people. Even when the process was documented, the real understanding of what to review, what to ignore, and how to explain exceptions often sat with a small group of subject matter experts. That model can work for a period of time. However, it becomes risky when workloads increase, people change roles, or an audit requires the team to reproduce decisions at scale. Connecting Monitoring With Compliance Execution Teams are not just looking for another point solution. They need a platform that connects data, guides work, reduces manual evidence assembly, and keeps NERC CIP programs audit-ready. That means closing the gaps utility contacts described. Teams need fewer disconnected reports, less spreadsheet coordination, clearer ownership, and a more reliable way to preserve decisions over time. That is where SigmaFlow workflow automation and SigmaFlow Beacon configuration monitoring fit together. In practice, SigmaFlow helps teams support: Multi-source data ingestion and lifecycle tracking Guided workflows for reviews, attestations, and exceptions Configuration monitoring connected to workflow-driven compliance execution Building A More Scalable Compliance Model Legacy platforms are not failing because they stopped working. Many teams have simply outgrown what those tools were built to do. When compliance depends on manual reports, disconnected evidence packages, cross-system data pulls, and institutional knowledge, the real issue is operational scale. The next step is to connect configuration monitoring with workflow-driven compliance operations. SigmaFlow and SigmaFlow Beacon support that shift by unifying monitoring, evidence management, and execution in one environment. Change detection is only one part of the compliance equation. body_text: Verity Prepare transforms reconciliation preparation, enabling finance teams to automate complex workflows with transparency, auditability, and human oversight LOS ANGELES, July 27, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- BlackLine, Inc. (Nasdaq: BL), the Agentic Financial Operations Platform™ for the Office of the CFO, today announced the general availability of Verity Prepare , a groundbreaking multi-agent AI system that brings governed automation to accounting's most manual and time-intensive close processes. Unlike standard text-generating AI assistants, Verity Prepare orchestrates a specialized digital workforce to autonomously analyze supporting documentation, match transactions, identify reconciling items, and assemble audit-ready reconciliations. By combining advanced multi-agent AI capability with transparent reasoning and human oversight, BlackLine accelerates the financial close while keeping accountants firmly in control through complete auditability. As finance organizations move beyond isolated AI assistants toward enterprise-scale AI deployment, the challenge is no longer whether AI can generate answers – it’s whether it can produce work that finance leaders trust enough to become part of the financial record. Following a successful early adopter program, Verity Prepare is now available, enabling organizations to confidently scale AI across one of accounting’s most demanding workflows while preserving the governance, transparency, and oversight required for enterprise finance. Transforming Reconciliation Preparation Preparing account reconciliations is far more than gathering supporting documents. Accountants must evaluate data from multiple systems, interpret structured and unstructured financial evidence, investigate discrepancies, determine appropriate reconciling items, document supporting rationale, and produce work that satisfies internal controls and external audit requirements. This combination of financial reasoning, documentation, and compliance has made reconciliation preparation one of the most difficult accounting processes to automate. Verity Prepare solves this challenge by replacing fragmented tasks with a fully coordinated AI workflow. Instead of relying on isolated tools, multiple specialized AI agents work together to execute the entire preparation process. They autonomously ingest supporting documents, isolate anomalies, write clear explanations for variances, and compile a comprehensive, audit-ready reconciliation package for human sign-off. By automating the entire preparation workflow – not just individual tasks – Verity Prepare dramatically reduces manual workloads. This shift enables accounting teams to accelerate the close, allowing finance professionals to focus on higher-value analysis, exception management, and safeguarding the integrity of the financial record. Built for the Standards of Finance Enterprise accounting demands more from AI than speed alone. Every AI-generated action must be transparent, explainable, traceable, and governed before it becomes part of the financial record. Verity Prepare was purpose-built for the governance expectations of enterprise finance, including the requirements of users, management, auditors, audit committees, and regulators. Every AI-generated recommendation includes transparent reasoning, confidence scoring, and a complete audit trail, allowing finance teams to understand how conclusions were reached before approving any outcome. Human judgment remains the final authority, ensuring AI enhances professional expertise rather than replacing it. “Finance organizations aren’t looking for AI that simply automates more tasks – they’re looking for AI they can trust with their most critical financial processes,” said Owen Ryan, CEO of BlackLine. “Trust isn’t achieved through autonomy alone. It comes from transparency, governance, and maintaining robust human oversight. Verity Prepare gives finance teams the confidence to deploy AI across one of accounting’s most complex processes while keeping professionals firmly in control.” Delivering Early Customer Impact Organizations are already realizing measurable results with Verity Prepare. Demonstrating how governed AI fundamentally transforms the financial close, early adopters have achieved up to a 92% reduction in manual reconciliation preparation time , demonstrating significant efficiency gains across the reconciliation process. “With BlackLine’s Verity AI, we’ve gone from concept to real-life practical use cases. We are excited to embrace where the future of work is going,” said Chris Giambra, Corporate Accounting at Delaware North. Advancing Agentic Financial Operations Verity Prepare represents another milestone in BlackLine’s vision for Agentic Financial Operations , where purpose-built AI capabilities orchestrate work across the Office of the CFO under a unified governance model. Rather than deploying isolated AI assistants, BlackLine enables organizations to coordinate specialized AI across finance, allowing complex processes to execute intelligently while maintaining enterprise-grade control. Verity Prepare advances the agentic close – transforming month-end from a series of manual, disconnected activities into a continuously orchestrated financial operation where AI prepares, matches, analyzes, and executes work while finance professionals provide the oversight, judgment, and accountability required to maintain the integrity of the financial record. Learn more about Verity Prepare at blackline.com/products/verity-ai/ . About BlackLine BlackLine (Nasdaq: BL) is the trust infrastructure for the AI era of finance: a future where finance drives the agentic era with intelligence, integrity, and trust rising together. The BlackLine Agentic Financial Operations Platform™, powered by Studio360 and Verity™ AI, is where the Office of the CFO scales AI across Record-to-Report, Invoice-to-Cash, and the processes where finance owns the controls and demands integrity at every step. By unifying data, embedding AI, and engineering trust into every action, BlackLine moves finance and accounting beyond reporting on the business to orchestrating it in real time. Supported by industry-leading R&D investment and world-class security practices, nearly 4,300 customers across multiple industries partner with BlackLine to lead their organizations into the future.
